content.title: About
content.content: Steamed catfish fillet is a tender piece of low‑fat fish with a high protein content. Steaming preserves most of its nutrients, making it a healthy and flavorful option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Catfish are freshwater fish native to rivers and lakes across North America and Asia.
The flesh has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a soft texture, popular in many Asian cuisines.
Steaming retains up to 90% of B‑vitamins and minerals such as phosphorus and selenium.
Catfish can survive in low‑oxygen water thanks to specialized breathing organs that allow them to gulp air.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Catfish provides about 18‑20 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other fish, catfish contains little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: It contains beneficial omega‑3 fatty acids that promote heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Catfish supplies vitamin B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a good source of phosphorus, selenium and potassium, supporting bone health, antioxidant defense and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including catfish.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Freshwater catfish can accumulate cadmium or mercury in polluted waters; choose products from reputable sources.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or insufficient cooking can allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steamed catfish fillet can be served on its own, sliced into salads, added to soups or rice dishes. It is often drizzled with soy sauce, lemon juice or fresh herbs to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fillet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor.
